questions.question: Pick three parts of the SERVQUAL model and explain how they help make service good. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Three parts of SERVQUAL model
  • & how they help service. U CO1 - Reliability: Consistency in delivering promised services, dependability, error-free performance.
  • Question Taxonomy CO Ans key
  • - Responsiveness: Promptness in helping customers,
  • quick resolution of complaints, willingness to assist.
  • - Assurance: Staff knowledge, courtesy, confidence
  • building, building trust.
  • - Tangibles: Cleanliness, professional appearance,
  • equipment, physical facilities, visual appeal.
  • - Empathy: Personalized attention, understanding
  • individual needs, caring attitude, approachable staff.
  • - Set service benchmarks, improve customer satisfaction,
  • identify gaps, enable targeted improvements, increase
  • repeat business.

questions.question: What are the tricky ethical situations that can come up when trying for excellent service, especially with customer information and making things personal? How can businesses handle these problems responsibly? / [CO1, CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Ethical issues with
  • service/personal customer info;
  • solutions?
  • An CO1, CO5
  • - Issues: Data privacy violation, unauthorized sharing,
  • misuse of confidential details.
  • - Solutions: Strong privacy policies, staff training,
  • encryption, consent forms, regular audits.
  • - Integrity: Ethical culture, honesty in handling information,
  • reporting breaches.
  • - Importance: Protects customer trust, legal compliance,
  • reputation management.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Talk about the ethical questions around dress codes and grooming rules at work. How can businesses balance needing a professional look with a person's freedom to express themselves? / [CO2, CO6]
questions.solution_html:
• Ethical issues with dress
  • code/grooming vs. self-expression. An CO2, CO6
  • - Dress code necessity: Brand standards,
  • professionalism, hygiene.
  • - Challenge: Diversity, cultural sensitivity, religious
  • expression, comfort.
  • - Balance: Flexible rules, inclusive policies, staff input,
  • respect for individuality.
  • - Example: Allowing cultural attire, considering gender -
  • neutral dress codes, accommodating disabilities.

questions.question: "The art of saying 'no' gracefully." Discuss strategies for effectively communicating limitations or denials to guests while maintaining a positive relationship and offering alternatives. / [CO3, CO4] [10x1 = 10]
questions.solution_html:
• Strategies for saying 'no'
  • gracefully. A CO3, CO4
  • - Polite denial: Positive language, soften the refusal,
  • express regret.
  • - Offer alternatives: Suggest other options, recommend
  • solutions.
  • - Empathetic explanation: Reasoning, show
  • understanding of guest’s position.
  • - Active listening: Acknowledge concerns, ensure guest
  • feels heard.
  • - Maintain relationship: Follow -up, express continued
  • support, keep the guest’s dignity intact.
